curriculum.title: Ecclesiastes and the Search for Meaning

core.big_idea: Ecclesiastes exposes the limits of life pursued without an adequate horizon beyond mortality.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.
Read in immediate context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Wisdom and Worship: Wisdom Literature within the Covenant, Kingdom, Wisdom, and Prophets cycle

claims.statement: Ecclesiastes opens by stressing transience and the repetitive limits of human striving under the sun.
The epilogue describes the Teacher as a careful wisdom instructor and concludes by calling people to fear God and keep His commands.
Taken together, these passages support the lesson’s big idea: Ecclesiastes exposes the limits of life pursued without an adequate horizon beyond mortality.

core.interpretation_skill: Locate on timeline; read immediate context; identify genre; separate observation and application

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from the passage that ecclesiastes exposes the limits of life pursued without an adequate horizon beyond mortality and locate the lesson on the whole-Bible timeline.
learning.extension_objective: Identify the immediate context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from a reasonable inference and application.
know: Ecclesiastes exposes the limits of life pursued without an adequate horizon beyond mortality.
The lesson belongs in Wisdom and Worship.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before interpretation.
Write one observation, one supported meaning, and one wise response from the passage.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with faithful trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

preparation.passage_context: Wisdom and Worship: Wisdom Literature within the Covenant, Kingdom, Wisdom, and Prophets cycle
text_observations: Ecclesiastes opens by stressing transience and the repetitive limits of human striving under the sun.
The epilogue describes the Teacher as a careful wisdom instructor and concludes by calling people to fear God and keep His commands.
interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.
Read this as Wisdom literature and account for its immediate literary setting.
Distinguish direct text, canonical synthesis, inference, and application.
theological_guardrails: Do not weaponize Ecclesiastes against students experiencing sadness or uncertainty. Its critique of human limits is wisdom reflection, not a diagnosis of depression or a denial of ordinary joys.
Questions and disagreement may be expressed without embarrassment or coercion.

accessibility.reading_level: Upper-primary guided reading with concrete supports
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the evidence, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
